raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bump the ROCm base images to AITER [v0.1.26](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/releases/tag/v0.1.26), and fix a test bug that the bump exposed.

With only the version bump, `test_aiter_fused_moe_mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_accuracy` failed in this PR's CI ([build 95937](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95937/list), step "(MI355 DPX) FP4 and INT4 MoE Kernels"). This is not a regression in v0.1.26. The test has always compared AITER's SwiGLU-OAI MoE against a SiLU reference. It only passed because of an AITER v0.1.25 dispatch bug that ran SiLU instead of SwiGLU. [ROCm/aiter#6478](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6478) fixes that bug in v0.1.26, so the kernel's output is now correct and the wrong reference fails.

## Claims

- `AITER_BRANCH` moves from `v0.1.25` to `v0.1.26` in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` and `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_72_base`.
- `ref_moe_forward` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` gains a `"swigluoai"` activation (alpha 1.702, clamp 7, `up + 1`, the same formula as CK-Tile's `ck_tile::moe::Swiglu`). The MI350 MXFP4 W4A16 accuracy test now uses it, so the test checks the activation it actually requests.
- With v0.1.26 and the test fix, all three commands of the "(MI355 DPX) FP4 and INT4 MoE Kernels" step pass on gfx950 (see Validation).

## Validation

All runs below used an MI355X (gfx950) with AITER v0.1.26 built from the tag.

| Command | v0.1.26, original test | v0.1.26, with the test fix |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k "mi350_mxfp4 or quant_scheme_support_matches_gfx950"` | 1 failed, 2 passed (accuracy: 21.39% pass, mean_abs 0.401) | 3 passed (accuracy: 100% pass, max_abs 0.0126, mean_abs 0.0016) |
| `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle -k AITER_MXFP4` | 3 passed | 3 passed |
| `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_flydsl_moe.py` | 30 passed | 30 passed |

The "original test" result for the first command reproduces the CI failure in [build 95937](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95937/list), which reported 20.97% pass and mean_abs 0.412 on an MI350X.

To show which activation the kernel computes, I ran the test's exact case (32 tokens, hidden 512, inter 1024, 4 experts, top-2, seed 11) on both AITER versions. Each run used no bias (as the test does) and a zero bias. A zero bias leaves the math unchanged but selects AITER's with-bias CK-Tile kernel. Each cell is the pass rate at atol = rtol = 0.1:

| AITER | Bias | vs SiLU reference | vs SwiGLU-OAI reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.25 | none | **100.00%** | 21.67% |
| v0.1.25 | zero | 21.39% | **100.00%** |
| v0.1.26 | none | 21.39% | **100.00%** |
| v0.1.26 | zero | 21.39% | **100.00%** |

On v0.1.25, a SwiGLU request without bias produced SiLU output. Every other combination, including v0.1.25 with a bias, produced SwiGLU-OAI.

**Model evals.** These are from this PR's CI ([build 95937](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95937/list), commit `9707fa4`, AITER v0.1.26 before the test fix; the test fix does not affect evals). Every eval step passed. A model passes when its measured score is at least the expected score minus the eval's tolerance.

GPQA, `:amd: (MI355) GPQA Eval (GPT-OSS)`, 4/4 passed:

| Config | Model | Measured | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b-rocm-baseline | openai/gpt-oss-20b | 0.5663 | 0.568 |
| gpt-oss-20b-rocm-quark-mxfp4-bf16-aiter | amd/gpt-oss-20b-w-mxfp4-a-bf16 | 0.5745 | 0.568 |
| gpt-oss-20b-rocm-quark-mxfp4-bf16-triton | amd/gpt-oss-20b-w-mxfp4-a-bf16 | 0.5530 | 0.568 |
| gpt-oss-20b-rocm-quark-mxfp4-fp8-triton | amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8 | 0.5562 | 0.568 |

<details>
<summary>GSM8K, `:amd: (MI355 DPX) LM Eval Small Models` (10 passed, 2 skipped) and `:amd: (MI300) LM Eval Small Models` (6 passed, 2 skipped)</summary>

| Config | MI355 | MI300 | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 | 0.3935 | 0.3821 | 0.375 |
| Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-INT8-CT | 0.3108 | 0.3108 | 0.31 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-nonuniform-CT | 0.7407 | 0.7339 | 0.74 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic | 0.6202 | 0.6262 | 0.60 |
| Qwen1.5-MoE-W4A16-CT | 0.4610 | 0.4481 | 0.45 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 | 0.7900 | 0.7779 | 0.72 |
| Qwen3-1.7B-MXFP4 | 0.2745 | — | 0.27 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 | 0.8772 | — | 0.89 |
| Laguna-XS.2-NVFP4 | 0.9022 | — | 0.90 |
| Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4 | 0.9151 | — | 0.90 |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16 and gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-mobile-ct are skipped on ROCm on both GPUs. The last four configs are only in the MI355 list.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** CK-Tile's `moe_dispatch` selects a kernel by `(activation, has_bias, split_k)`, and `has_bias` comes from whether a bias tensor is passed. In AITER ≤ v0.1.25, `gen_instances.py` built SwiGLU kernels only with `has_bias=true`. A SwiGLU call with no bias therefore reached `moe_gemm1_heuristic_dispatcher<..., Swiglu, false, ...>`, which had no specialization. Its primary template is `static MoeKernel dispatch(...) {}`, an empty body with no return, which is undefined behavior. In practice it ran a SiLU kernel. The test calls `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` with `MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI` and no bias, so it was scored against that SiLU result and matched. [ROCm/aiter#6478](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6478), which is in v0.1.26, generates the missing no-bias SwiGLU kernel and makes the unspecialized dispatcher throw. The kernel now computes gpt-oss SwiGLU, so the test's SiLU reference fails.

**Impact on real models.** gpt-oss checkpoints have expert biases, so they take the with-bias kernel, which computed SwiGLU on v0.1.25 as well (zero-bias row above). Any caller that used SwiGLU without bias on AITER ≤ v0.1.25 was silently getting SiLU. This PR fixes that path for them.

**Why the test fix is in this PR.** The corrected reference fails on v0.1.25 (no-bias row above), so it has to land together with the bump.

**Duplicate check.** No open vLLM PR references this test or AITER v0.1.26 (`gh pr list --search "mi350_mxfp4_w4a16"` and `--search "aiter v0.1.26"`). On the AITER side, #6478 and #6620 are both already in v0.1.26, and neither changes this test's no-bias path.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the root cause and draft the test fix and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above on MI355X hardware.

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

@@ -222,6 +222,10 @@ def ref_moe_forward(
             act = F.silu(gate) * up
         elif activation == "gelu":
             act = F.gelu(gate) * up
+        elif activation == "swigluoai":
+            gate = gate.clamp(max=7.0)
+            up = up.clamp(-7.0, 7.0)
+            act = gate * torch.sigmoid(1.702 * gate) * (up + 1)
         else:
             raise ValueError(f"Unknown activation: {activation}")
         output[expert_mask] = act @ w2_f[expert_idx].T

         case.topk_ids,

     )
